input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The new accounting export tool on Windows almost certainly writes CRLF (`\r\n`) line endings. `parseStatement` splits the file only on `"\n"`, so each line (including the header) keeps a trailing `"\r"`. That makes the last header column become `"description\r"` instead of `"description"`, so `REQUIRED_COLUMNS.some(... !header.includes(column))` fails for `"description"` and `assertShape` throws `errors.rowShape` for the header itself (index 0 → reported as row 1) — exactly matching the reported symptom of every upload failing on row 1 regardless of content. The fix should normalize/strip `\r` from line endings (e.g. split on `/\r?\n/` or trim each line) before parsing the header and rows.
